extracted.intended_audience: scholars, authors, librarians, and committees evaluating journals/publishers for submission, editorial service, or assessment
extracted.subtask_description: Using Beall's archived list to determine whether a publisher or its journals are potentially predatory; includes brief usage instructions and pointers to additional evaluation resources. The page is an archival dataset of publisher names with notes and links rather than a full criterion glossary.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to use this list / basic lookup instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: First, find the journal’s publisher – it is usually written at the bottom of the journal’s webpage or in the “About” section. Then simply enter the publisher’s name or its URL in the search box above. If the journal does not have a publisher use the Standalone Journals list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical step-by-step instruction for users: locate publisher information on a journal site and search this list (or Standalone Journals if no publisher).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption about journals under listed publishers
rubrics_metrics.description: All journals published by a predatory publisher are potentially predatory unless stated otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a publisher appears on this list, treat all of its journals as suspect by default; check for explicit exceptions noted on the list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of this archival list (updates policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: This is an archived version of the Beall’s list – a list of potential predatory publishers created by a librarian Jeffrey Beall. We will only update links and add notes to this list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page is maintained in an archival mode: links and notes may be updated but the list itself is presented as an archive rather than a continuously re-evaluated formal registry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of non-open-access publishers with predatory practices
rubrics_metrics.description: In a few cases, non-open access publishers whose practices match those of predatory publishers have been added to the list as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list is not restricted strictly to open‑access publishers—publishers with similar problematic practices may be included even if they are not OA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to read reviews and decide for yourself
rubrics_metrics.description: We recommend that scholars read the available reviews, assessments and descriptions provided here, and then decide for themselves whether they want to submit articles, serve as editors or on editorial boards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users are advised to consult linked reviews/assessments and exercise personal/professional judgement before engaging with listed publishers or journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for tenure and promotion committees
rubrics_metrics.description: We hope that tenure and promotion committees can also decide for themselves how importantly or not to rate articles published in these journals in the context of their own institutional standards and/or geocultural locus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional evaluators should apply their own standards and contextual judgement when weighing publications in journals/publishers listed here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat about changing publisher practices / timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: We emphasize that journal publishers and journals change in their business and editorial practices over time. This list is kept up-to-date to the best extent possible but may not reflect sudden, unreported, or unknown enhancements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify current publisher/journal practices independently; presence on the list may not reflect later improvements and absence may not reflect new misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pointer to Beall’s criteria (external)
rubrics_metrics.description: The criteria for determining predatory publishers are here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This page does not reproduce Beall’s detailed criteria; users should follow the provided link to review the underlying criteria used to label publishers as potentially predatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Useful external evaluation resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Useful pages: List of journals falsely claiming to be indexed by DOAJ; DOAJ: Journals added and removed; Nonrecommended medical periodicals; Retraction Watch; Flaky Academic Journals Blog; List of scholarly publishing stings; Journal Evaluation Tool; JCR Master Journal List; DOAJ Journal Search; Think Check Submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page recommends consulting established external tools and resources (DOAJ, JCR, Think Check Submit, Retraction Watch, etc.) as part of evaluating journals/publishers; these are offered as complementary checks rather than part of the list itself.
